3DEP elevation with a provisional 8,000–12,000 ft host belt (engineering)

Annual NLCD land cover for forest/open cover (weights unchanged)

candidates.why: Resolved taxon concept with a specific spruce host association (Engelmann spruce at higher elevations) plus Colorado observational range support.
modelUses: July–September calendar from Colorado iNaturalist observation months (observational, not surveyed)
mapped spruce/fir classes with a heavy spruce weight (source-supported host, engineering weight)
NLCD tree canopy as forest-structure evidence (canopy weight declared earlier; now sourced)

candidates.why: GTR-710 separates non-burn from fire-associated morels and describes the Interior West including Colorado; a defensible model must not treat morels as one ecological unit.
modelUses: June–July calendar from the published snowmelt/elevation progression (engineering calendar, not a published Colorado phenology)
mapped conifer and aspen host classes
Annual NLCD land cover for mapped forest cover (weights unchanged; no canopy weight)
missing: a snowmelt-date dataset (only an elevation-and-season proxy is used)
a published Colorado non-burn morel survey

candidates.why: Real MTBS perimeters are now published for a Colorado tile, so a disturbance-dependent target can be scored without inventing fire evidence.
modelUses: years-since-fire response: 1 year strongest, 2 years moderate, 3 years weak (sourced direction, engineering weights)
prior-year fire association in high-elevation Picea/Abies stands (McFarlane et al. 2005, Idaho and Montana)
Annual NLCD land cover for mapped forest cover (weights unchanged; no canopy weight)
candidates.evidenceGapRule: The target declares requiresDisturbance with an explicit evidenceGapCap. When the fire layer is unavailable or no mapped perimeter applies, the disturbance component stays missing, confidence drops, the band states that fire evidence is unavailable, and the score is capped. Absence of a mapped perimeter is never scored as a negative signal.
missing: a per-fire severity response (MTBS publishes no per-perimeter severity class, so severity stays null and applies no penalty)
